mechanism: Semantic colour token enum

what_is_missing: The theme *table* half exists; the semantic *indirection* half does not, and the table itself lives in two places. src/nimculus/settings.nim:31 declares ThemeColors (~48 string fields) and registerBuiltinThemes at :523 fills the dark palette (:525-547) and light palette (:551-...) — this is real and complete. But no call site names a meaning: macos_platform.m:942 themeRoleColor(NSString *key, NSColor *fallback) takes a raw string key, resolves it through themeRole (:890) against the theme JSON, and on miss falls through to themeTokenFallback (:908), which is a SECOND copy of the palettes as ObjC literals — lightValues at :910-923 and darkValues at :924-937 re-state 31 of the same hex strings already in settings.nim:525/551. acceptance: (1) A Nim `UiColor` enum exists with one arm per token consumed by the platform layer, and `proc color(c: UiColor, theme: ThemeColors): string` with an exhaustive case — compilation fails if an arm is added without a mapping. (3) Unit test: for both built-in themes every UiColor arm resolves to a 7- or 9-character '#'-prefixed string. (4) Regression pin: under the built-in dark theme the hover surface for a chrome button resolves to #363c46, not #dce0e5. Checked with a folder open (chrome buttons only exist in the workspace chrome, not in the single-file window).

what_is_missing: Nimculus uses macOS 14 CADisplayLink per view (macos_platform.m:9545-9567, preferredFrameRateRange clamped to 60..min(120, screen.maximumFramesPerSecond) at :9556-9558), which is a legitimate simplification of Zed's CVDisplayLink registry and should not be reverted. The defect is in the fallback. requestRedraw (macos_platform.m:9529) computes displayLinkCanRender from window visible && !miniaturized && occlusionState & Visible (:9533-9538); when that is false it calls [self stopDisplayLink] (:9541) and draws synchronously. Nothing in that path ever restarts the link: restartDisplayLinkIfNeeded (:9576) early-returns when !displayLinkRunning (:9577), so the only restarts are the window-delegate notifications at macos_platform.m:11057, :11061, :11065, :11071, :12197 and viewDidMoveToWindow at :10810. So a single requestRedraw during a transient non-visible occlusionState (which AppKit reports right after makeKeyAndOrderFront at macos_platform.m:12163) permanently demotes the process to synchronous drawing until the next becomeKey/expose notification. Zed never draws synchronously off the link except in display_layer. Second gap, lower priority: Zed shares one link per CGDirectDisplayID so N windows tick once; Nimculus is per-view, which is invisible today because there is exactly one window (macos_platform.m:12111).
acceptance: After a synchronous-fallback draw, the link is re-armed: a native-contract test nimculus_platform_validate_display_link_recovery forces displayLinkCanRender false once, calls requestRedraw, then restores visibility and asserts self.displayLinkRunning is YES within one runloop turn without any NSWindow notification being posted. Additionally NimculusPlatformMetrics.frame_count (contracts.h:14) must advance by at least 30 over a 1.0s idle-with-dirty period sourced from the link, with last_frame_time_ms recorded on every one of those frames.

acceptance: 1. A blurred shadow pipeline exists and the paint command carries blur_radius and corner_radii: with a shadow of blur_radius 12 under the command palette, the captured PNG shows a monotonically decreasing alpha ramp over at least 10 device pixels measured outward from the palette's bottom edge at its horizontal centre — today it is a single hard step from panel colour to a 0.35-black rect at +3,+3. 2. No paint kind resolves its own colour from an ObjC literal: grep for NSColor inside the paint-kind dispatch (macos_platform.m:2400-2600) returns zero hits, every colour arriving in the NimculusPaintCommand struct. 3. Wavy diagnostic underline: with one error diagnostic on a line, sampling the underline row across 40 device pixels yields at least 4 alternations in y of the top-most inked pixel; today it is constant. Measured with One Dark, single file open, tools/ui_test.sh capture conditions.

mechanism: IME arbitration: who sees a key first, the keybinding matcher or the input context
zed_reference: crates/gpui_macos/src/window.rs:2121 (handle_key_event), :2094 (is_ime_input_source_active), :2848 (do_command_by_selector), decision comment at :2057-2083
what_is_missing: Both participants exist but the arbitration is a fixed order, not a per-key decision. Today: keyDown: (macos_platform.m:10737) calls logInput, which offers the raw NSEvent to g_shortcut_callback first (macos_platform.m:4101-4104) and, only if that returns false, calls interpretKeyEvents: unconditionally (macos_platform.m:10739). So shortcuts always win over the IME. Zed decides per key from four inputs — currently composing, key char printable, modifiers, and whether the current TIS source is a non-ASCII-capable input mode — and there is no TIS call anywhere in macos_platform.m (grep for TISCopyCurrentKeyboardInputSource returns nothing), so the ime_source_active input simply does not exist. Second half: doCommandBySelector: (macos_platform.m:10897) maps 30 selectors to fire-and-forget string commands via g_command_callback and returns void (:10897-10927). Zed's version re-dispatches the stashed keystroke as a KeyDown and records whether it was handled (window.rs:2848). Nimculus therefore cannot tell an unhandled command from a handled one, and cannot fall back. Consequence, which is the case Zed's comment enumerates: with the Japanese IME active, a multi-stroke binding whose first key is a printable ASCII char consumes the key before composition starts.
acceptance: A pure decision function ime_should_see_key(composing, key_char_is_printable, modifiers, ime_source_is_non_ascii) lives in Nim and is called back through contracts.h; the .m contributes only the TIS query. Unit-test the function over the full 2x2x2 truth table plus the modifier cases and require it to match Zed's window.rs:2121-2160 branch-for-branch. Then extend nimculus_platform_validate_ime_command_dispatch (platform.h:59) so doCommandBySelector: returns a bool: with a synthetic composing state and the Japanese input source reported active, a printable ASCII keyDown must reach setMarkedText: and must NOT reach g_shortcut_callback; with the ASCII input source active the same keystroke must reach g_shortcut_callback first. Both directions must be asserted — testing only one leaves the current behaviour passing.

what_is_missing: Zed stores one `Arc<Mutex<MacWindowState>>` in an ivar on both the NSWindow and the NSView; every callback recovers it, and the re-entrancy discipline is to `take()` the callback out of the state and drop the lock before invoking it (window.rs:2821-2830 is the canonical example). Nimculus has no ivar and no per-window state object at all: src/nimnui/platform/macos/macos_platform.m carries 617 file-scope `static` declarations that together play the role of MacWindowState — g_editor_rect (:245), g_editor_scroll_line (:294), g_editor_text (:385), the pipeline/atlas globals (:1285-1308, :1455-1457), and so on. The concrete cost is already in the tree: because 'the editor state' is a single set of globals rather than per-pane state, the .m has to fake a second pane by swapping the globals in and out — swapEditorTextState (:769) is called in pairs at :778/:780, :3086/:3096, :8953/:8980, and firstRectForCharacterRange (:11235) has to call it twice (:11251, :11258) just to answer an IME geometry question about the secondary pane. Nothing here is a Nim-language obstacle: src/nimnui/platform/dispatcher.nim:30-33 already pins a Nim `ref object` with GC_ref and hands it to ObjC as `void *`, which is exactly the Arc-in-an-ivar trick.
acceptance: Add a `NimculusWindowState` struct in macos_platform.m plus an ivar on NimculusMetalView and on the window class, with getWindowState()/dropWindowState() mirroring window.rs:2091-2106, and move the editor-text/rect/scroll/IME group of globals into it — specifically the ones swapEditorTextState touches. Measurable acceptance, all three required: (1) swapEditorTextState and every call site of it are deleted — `grep -c swapEditorTextState src/nimnui/platform/macos/macos_platform.m` returns 0; (2) `grep -c '^static ' src/nimnui/platform/macos/macos_platform.m` drops from 617 to at most 590; (3) nimculus_platform_validate_secondary_annotation_isolation and nimculus_platform_validate_ime_composition (declared in src/nimnui/platform/macos/platform.h) still return true, and firstRectForCharacterRange answers for the secondary pane without any global save/restore — assert this by adding a check to tests/test_platform_contract.nim that both validators pass while two panes hold different text. Do not introduce a lock-free shortcut: the take-callback-then-release pattern of window.rs:2821-2830 must be reproduced for the frame and input callbacks.

mechanism: presents-with-transaction during synchronous redraw
zed_reference: references/zed/crates/gpui_macos/src/window.rs:2818-2832 (display_layer: set_presents_with_transaction(true) + stop_display_link, draw synchronously, then false + start_display_link), :2708-2716 (the same pair around the live-resize path), references/zed/crates/gpui_macos/src/metal_renderer.rs:374-380 (set_presents_with_transaction forwards to the CAMetalLayer), :479-487 (commit + wait_until_scheduled + drawable.present() when the flag is set, present_drawable + commit otherwise)
what_is_missing: Zed swaps the presentation mode whenever AppKit — not the display link — drives the frame. In presentsWithTransaction mode the drawable is presented inside the layer transaction, so a live resize cannot show a half-resized drawable. Nimculus has neither half of this. NimculusMetalView implements no displayLayer: at all (`grep -n displayLayer src/nimnui/platform/macos/macos_platform.m` returns nothing), so AppKit's synchronous redraw path never reaches the renderer; and drawFrame (src/nimnui/platform/macos/macos_platform.m:10702) unconditionally ends with `[command presentDrawable:drawable]` at :10985, with no presentsWithTransaction branch and no commit/waitUntilScheduled/present alternative. Frames come only from the CADisplayLink path (:9774, :9792) or the synchronous fallback at :9792, neither of which is coordinated with the layer transaction. Resize therefore presents out of band with the layer, which is the exact tear Zed's comment structure exists to avoid.
acceptance: Implement displayLayer: on NimculusMetalView, and give drawFrame a presentsWithTransaction branch that does commit + waitUntilScheduled + [drawable present] exactly as metal_renderer.rs:479-483, keeping [command presentDrawable:] for the display-link path. Numeric gate: add nimculus_platform_validate_presents_with_transaction to platform.h/platform.nim returning true only when, inside a scripted live-resize of the window from 960x720 to 1280x800, (a) displayLayer: was entered at least once, (b) metalLayer.presentsWithTransaction was YES for every frame delivered from displayLayer: and NO for every frame delivered from the display link, and (c) the display link was stopped for the duration of each synchronous frame. Additionally capture the resize with tools/window_capture.swift and run tools/bitdiff.sh across consecutive frames: no captured frame may contain a horizontal seam, i.e. no scanline where the row-to-row pixel delta exceeds 5% of the frame width while its neighbours are below 1%. Report the measured frame time from drawFrame during the resize; it must stay under 16.6ms so the synchronous path does not trade tearing for stutter.

mechanism: Glyph rasterization with subpixel variants and dilation
zed_reference: references/zed/crates/gpui_macos/src/text_system.rs:421-434 (raster_bounds, bounds.dilate(DevicePixels(1))), :436-528 (rasterize_glyph: +1px per non-zero subpixel axis at :446-451, gray kCGImageAlphaOnly vs RGBA premultiplied at :456-478, subpixel positioning on and quantization off at :497-500, dilation as gray luminance dilation*0.25 with should_smooth_fonts at :502-508, subpixel_shift applied to the draw origin at :510-521, RGBA-premultiplied to BGRA-straight swizzle at :523-527)
what_is_missing: Nimculus already has most of the key, but not the rasterization behaviour. NimculusRenderGlyphParams (src/nimnui/platform/macos/macos_platform.m:1338-1348) carries subpixel_variant_x/y, subpixel_rendering and dilation, and the Nim mirror src/nimnui/text.nim:123-134 (GlyphKey) has the same fields — but atlasEntryForGlyph (:3656) constructs the key with `isEmoji ? 1 : 0, 0, 0` (:3660-3663), i.e. subpixel_rendering and dilation are hardcoded to zero and never reach the bitmap. In the raster body (:3676-3746) there is no CGContextSetShouldSmoothFonts, no CGContextSetAllowsFontSubpixelPositioning / SetShouldSubpixelPositionFonts, no CGContextSetAllowsFontSubpixelQuantization / SetShouldSubpixelQuantizeFonts — `grep -rn 'SmoothFonts|SubpixelQuantiz|SubpixelPositio' src/` returns nothing — so CoreGraphics rasterizes at its defaults, with quantization left on, which defeats the four X-variants that NIMCULUS_SUBPIXEL_VARIANTS_X (:1289) is asking for. Padding also differs in kind: Zed dilates the measured bounds by 1px on all sides (text_system.rs:433) and then adds one extra pixel only on an axis whose subpixel variant is non-zero (:446-451); Nimculus uses a flat `padding = 1` on both axes for every variant (:3686-3688). Finally the emoji path keeps premultiplied BGRA (kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedFirst | kCGBitmapByteOrder32Little, :3730-3731) where Zed converts to straight alpha (:523-527). None of this is exposed through src/nimnui/platform/contracts.h — there is no rasterize_glyph entry point — so the Nim framework cannot own the cache key even though src/nimnui/text.nim:123 defines it.
acceptance: Reproduce Zed's raster settings, not an approximation of them. (1) atlasEntryForGlyph takes subpixelRendering and dilation as real parameters and puts them in the key; (2) the bitmap context sets should/allows subpixel positioning YES and should/allows subpixel quantization NO, and for dilation > 0 sets CGContextSetShouldSmoothFonts(YES) with gray fill luminance dilation*0.25 exactly as text_system.rs:502-508; (3) padding follows Zed: dilate bounds by 1px per side, then +1px on the X axis only when subpixel_variant_x > 0 and on Y only when subpixel_variant_y > 0. Measurable gates: rasterizing the same glyph at variants x=0..3 must produce four atlas entries whose coverage centroids differ by 0.25 +/- 0.05 device pixels per step — assert this numerically in tests/test_ui_text.nim by reading back the atlas bytes; entries for x=0 and x=1 must have widths differing by exactly 1; and rasterizing with dilation=0 vs dilation=2 must raise mean alpha coverage of the same glyph by at least 8% while the bounding box is unchanged. Report the four centroid values in the commit message.

mechanism: Font fallback cascade and OpenType features
zed_reference: references/zed/crates/gpui_macos/src/open_type.rs:34-74 (apply_features_and_fallbacks: kCTFontFeatureSettingsAttribute always, kCTFontCascadeListAttribute when the user list is non-empty, then CTFontCreateCopyWithAttributes), :77-99 (generate_feature_array), :102-152 (generate_fallback_array: user fallbacks carry the base font's weight and slant traits), :155-176 (append_system_fallbacks: CTFontCopyDefaultCascadeListForLanguages filtered to descriptors that have a font path)
what_is_missing: This one is half-built rather than absent, and the half that is missing is the deterministic part. src/nimnui/platform/macos/macos_platform.m has generateFeatureArray (:2798), generateFallbackArray (:2839) and appendSystemFallbacks (:2820), and editorFont (:2911-2925) assembles kCTFontFeatureSettingsAttribute plus kCTFontCascadeListAttribute into a descriptor. But :2911-2916 only attaches the cascade list `if (fallbacks.count > 0)` — with an empty user fallback list Nimculus never installs a cascade list at all, so the system cascade (appendSystemFallbacks, :2820-2836) is skipped and missing glyphs resolve through CoreText's per-call substitution, which is exactly the non-determinism open_type.rs:155 exists to remove. Zed reaches append_system_fallbacks through generate_fallback_array on every font that has features applied. Second gap: the whole mechanism is bolted to editor-font globals (g_editor_font_fallbacks :1457, g_editor_font_feature_tags/_values :1455-1456) and is unreachable for any other font — src/nimnui/platform/contracts.h:98-101 declares NimculusEditorFontFeature but src/nimnui/platform/macos/platform.h exposes no general per-run font-config entry point, while the layout path nimculus_platform_layout_line (platform.h:3) takes NimculusPlatformFontRun with no feature or fallback field. Third: appendSystemFallbacks filters on kCTFontURLAttribute (:2828) where Zed filters on desc.font_path() — equivalent in intent, worth confirming it produces the same descriptor count.
acceptance: (1) editorFont must build the cascade list unconditionally, matching open_type.rs:34-74 — the system cascade is installed even when editor.fontFallbacks is empty. Gate: with editor.fontFallbacks unset, CFArrayGetCount of the installed kCTFontCascadeListAttribute must be >= 1 and must equal the count appendSystemFallbacks produces; assert via a new nimculus_platform_validate_font_cascade in platform.h/platform.nim. (2) With editor.fontFallbacks = ["Hiragino Sans"], the array must be exactly 1 + system-count entries with the user entry at index 0, and its kCTFontWeightTrait/kCTFontSlantTrait must equal the base font's — read them back and compare to CTFontCopyTraits of the base font within 1e-6. (3) Rendering the string "fi -> == 漢字🙂" at 15pt must produce zero .notdef glyphs (glyph id 0) through nimculus_platform_layout_line, and with editor.fontFeatures {"calt": false} the glyph count for "->" must be 2 while with calt enabled the ligating face yields 1 — assert both counts in tests/test_ui_text.nim. Report the cascade-array counts for both the empty and non-empty fallback cases.

mechanism: Keyboard layout identity and per-layout key-equivalent remapping
zed_reference: references/zed/crates/gpui_macos/src/keyboard.rs:13-21 (MacKeyboardLayout id/name, MacKeyboardMapper key_equivalents), :32-51 (map_key_equivalent substitutes the binding character when use_key_equivalents), :53-77 (MacKeyboardLayout::new reads kTISPropertyInputSourceID and kTISPropertyLocalizedName from TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource), :88-110 (the comment explaining why the tables exist), :110-1502 (the per-layout (char, char) tables — 1502 lines total), references/zed/crates/gpui_macos/src/platform.rs:148 and :944 (on_keyboard_layout_change), :213-214 and :1018 (the layout and mapper are platform state, rebuilt on layout change)
what_is_missing: Nimculus makes no TIS call anywhere: `grep -rn 'TISCopy|TISGetInputSourceProperty|NSTextInputContextKeyboard' src/` returns nothing, so there is no layout id, no layout name, and no notification observer for NSTextInputContextKeyboardSelectionDidChange. The keybinding matcher that would consume the mapping does exist and is layout-blind: src/nimnui/commands.nim:21-33 defines Keystroke/Shortcut, :79-85 matchKeystrokes compares raw keyCode plus modifiers, :121-137 bindingsForInput/resolve, and keymaps are user-configurable through settings (src/nimculus/settings.nim:455-462 validates the "keymap" array, :1015 reads it). So on a German QWERTZ or Finnish layout a keymap entry for cmd-[ matches nothing and displays nothing, which is precisely the failure keyboard.rs:88-110 documents. Zed also re-reads the layout on change and rebuilds the mapper (platform.rs:213-214, :944); Nimculus has no equivalent because it has no layout at all.
acceptance: Large because of the ~1400 lines of tables; port them, do not invent a smaller scheme — the tables are the mechanism. Minimal first step: (1) add nimculus_platform_keyboard_layout(char *id, uint32_t id_cap, char *name, uint32_t name_cap) in the .m over TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource plus an observer on NSTextInputContextKeyboardSelectionDidChangeNotification that fires a layout-changed callback; gate: on a US layout the returned id is exactly "com.apple.keylayout.ABC" or "com.apple.keylayout.US", and switching input sources fires the callback exactly once per switch. (2) In src/nimnui/commands.nim add `const keyEquivalents: Table[string, seq[(char, char)]]` transcribed verbatim from keyboard.rs:110-1502 and a mapKeyEquivalent proc mirroring keyboard.rs:32-51. Gate, checkable without hardware: a unit test asserts the table has one entry per layout id present in keyboard.rs (count them and pin the number in the test), and asserts three specific substitutions byte-for-byte against the Rust source — ABC-AZERTY '!'->'1', German '['->'ö' and ']'->'ä', Finnish '['->'ö'. (3) resolve() consults mapKeyEquivalent when a keymap entry sets use_key_equivalents; gate: with the layout forced to German, a keymap binding on cmd-[ matches a keystroke whose character is 'ö' and reports its display string as cmd-ö.

mechanism: Display enumeration and coordinate space

what_is_missing: Nimculus has no display abstraction on either side of the boundary. acceptance: Add `NimculusDisplay { uint32 id; uint8 uuid[16]; float bounds_x/y/width/height; float visible_x/y/width/height; float scale; }` to contracts.h with a Nim mirror in contracts.nim, plus nimculus_platform_displays(NimculusDisplay *out, uint32_t cap) and nimculus_platform_primary_display(NimculusDisplay *out) implemented over CGGetActiveDisplayList / NSScreen[0]'s NSScreenNumber exactly as display.rs:28-65. Numeric gates, all asserted in tests/test_platform_contract.nim: (1) the returned count equals NSScreen.screens.count; (2) the primary display's bounds equal CGDisplayBounds of the id read from NSScreen[0], to within 0.5pt; (3) every uuid is 16 non-zero bytes and is stable across two consecutive calls; (4) the coordinate flip is correct — for the primary display, visible_y equals screen.frame.height - visibleFrame.origin.y - visibleFrame.height + screen.frame.origin.y to within 0.5pt, which on a machine with the menu bar visible means visible_y is at least 24 and strictly greater than bounds_y; (5) visible_height is strictly less than bounds_height. Do not return AppKit rects unflipped and fix it at the call site — the flip belongs at the boundary, as in display.rs:133.

mechanism: Window blur / vibrancy background

Callers are on their own, and three of them get it wrong: src/nimculus/main.nim:9291 and :9314 (workspace Replace / Replace All) call `openDocument(match.path)` then `target.save()` with no registry lookup at all, so replacing inside a file that is open and dirty reads the on-disk text, writes it back, and silently discards the user's unsaved edits while the tab keeps showing stale content; src/nimculus/main.nim:8515 reloads via `openDocument(path)` likewise. src/nimculus/main.nim:3629 (LSP workspace edit) does consult tabIndexForPath, but because FileDocument is a value object (editor_app.nim:14, holding PieceTable by value, editor_buffer.nim:21) it must hand-copy the result back at main.nim:3651 `editorSession.tabs[tabIndex].document = target` — the dedup guarantee is a per-callsite convention, not a property of the store. Second, there is no equivalent of path_to_buffer_id being rekeyed on rename: editor_app.nim:142 `save*` updates `document.path` (and comments that it does so for identity) but never touches session.tabRegistry, so after Save As the registry still maps the OLD path to the tab and does not map the new one — only addTab (:215) and moveTab (:318) ever rebuild it, and the stale entry survives until tabIndexForPath's linear fallback (:392) papers over it. Third, there is no entry-id index: FileDocument already carries `externalIdentity` (editor_app.nim:22, the filesystem identity) which is the natural ProjectEntryId analogue, but nothing indexes by it, so a rename on disk cannot update a buffer's path without reopening. Fourth, there is no BufferStoreEvent channel of any kind — nothing corresponding to BufferAdded / BufferDropped / BufferChangedFilePath, so LSP, git and the tab bar each rediscover changes by polling. Fifth, load coalescing is absent by construction: every openDocument is an independent synchronous readFile.
acceptance: New file tests/test_buffer_store.nim (auto-discovered by tests/test_runner.nim:16) must pass under `nimble test` and must contain at least these assertions against a new single entry point `proc openBuffer*(session: var EditorSession; path: string): int` in src/nimculus/editor_app.nim (returning the tab index, doing the get_by_path fast path before any filesystem read) plus `proc bufferEvents*(session: var EditorSession): seq[BufferStoreEvent]` where `BufferStoreEvent = object case kind: bufferAdded|bufferDropped|bufferChangedFilePath`: (1) Dedup: write /tmp fixture a.txt with "one"; `let i = session.openBuffer(p)`; overwrite the file on disk with "two"; `let j = session.openBuffer(p)`; assert j == i and session.tabs[i].document.buffer.toString() == "one" (proving the second call performed zero filesystem reads). (2) Dedup survives dirt: after openBuffer, applyEdits so isDirty is true, then openBuffer the same path again; assert the index is unchanged and isDirty is still true. (3) Symlink/alias identity: openBuffer("/tmp/x/a.txt") and openBuffer("/private/tmp/x/a.txt") return the same index and session.tabs.len increases by exactly 1. (4) Rekey on Save As: openBuffer(a.txt) -> index i; save the tab as b.txt; assert session.tabIndexForPath(a.txt) == -1, session.tabIndexForPath(b.txt) == i, session.tabRegistry.len == 1, and that exactly one bufferChangedFilePath event was emitted carrying the old path. (5) Entry-id index: after openBuffer(a.txt), rename a.txt to c.txt on disk and feed the rename through the store keyed on FileDocument.externalIdentity; assert session.tabIndexForPath(c.txt) == i, session.tabs.len unchanged, and session.tabs[i].document.buffer.version is byte-identical to before (no reload). (6) Events: opening emits exactly one bufferAdded; closing emits exactly one bufferDropped; opening the same path twice emits exactly one bufferAdded total. what_is_missing: There is no sidebar container in Nimculus — the word 'sidebar' does not appear in src/nimculus/workspace_ui.nim at all. What exists is (a) a dock, and (b) a mode enum. src/nimculus/workspace_ui.nim:109 has `leftDock, bottomDock, rightDock: DockState` with per-panel widths (:75 comment 'Width is stored per panel in WorkspaceUiState, not on the dock') and defaults DefaultLeftDockWidth 240 (:127) / DefaultDockMinimumSize 160 (:133), and src/nimculus/main.nim:1106 declares `EditorSidebarMode = enum sidebarOutline, sidebarFiles, sidebarGitHistory, sidebarGitStatus, sidebarGitBranches, sidebarWorkspaceSearch, sidebarDebugger` with a single global `var editorSidebarMode = sidebarFiles` (main.nim:1115) mapped back onto PanelKind by workspacePanelForSidebarMode (main.nim:1120). Concrete divergences from Zed's container: (1) The sidebar is not a registered object with its own lifetime — there is no analogue of MultiWorkspace.register_sidebar (multi_workspace.rs:389) or the SidebarHandle vtable (multi_workspace.rs:159); the sidebar is whatever the dock happens to contain, decided by a module-level var in main.nim. (2) It has no width of its own: main.nim:452 `const MacNativeSidebarMinimumDockWidth = 128'f32` and :457 `let sidebarWidth = if sidebarOnRight: rightDockWidth else: leftDockWidth` derive it from the dock, so Zed's 200/300/800 clamp (sidebar.rs:104, applied in set_width at sidebar.rs:7675) has no place to live. (3) There is no per-sidebar serialized state blob — sidebar.rs:7715 serialized_state / :7726 restore_serialized_state round-trip {width, active_view} as opaque JSON owned by the sidebar; Nimculus persists dock geometry and the panel enum ordinal separately (workspace_ui.nim:17-19 documents that ordinals are persisted, which is itself the bug Zed avoids with persistent_name strings). (4) There is no side selection: sidebar.rs:7690 reads SidebarSide from settings and multi_workspace.rs:66 offers the left/right context menu; main.nim:455 infers `sidebarOnRight` from which dock happens to be open. (5) There is no entry list model: SidebarContents (sidebar.rs:479) is a flat `entries: Vec<ListEntry>` of Thread / Terminal / ProjectHeader with project_header_indices, notified_threads/notified_terminals badge sets, an EntryShape identity key (sidebar.rs:492) that preserves measured row heights across rebuilds, and — decisively — `selection: Option<usize>` (keyboard focus) kept SEPARATE from `active_entry: Option<ActiveEntry>` (sidebar.rs:744-750, with the explicit comment that they are not the same). Nimculus has exactly one selection index, reached through platformSetEditorSidebarSelection (main.nim:1129-1132), so the keyboard cursor and the active item cannot diverge. (6) There is no notification state: has_notifications (sidebar.rs:7682) has no counterpart; main.nim:1284-1317 SidebarLineFlag* are git per-line decorations, not entry badges. (7) There is no cross-workspace source: Zed's entries come from MultiWorkspace across every open workspace (sidebar.rs:800 MultiWorkspaceEvent subscriptions); Nimculus has one activeWorkspace. (8) The rows are drawn by AppKit inside src/nimnui/platform/macos/macos_platform.m via nimculus_platform_set_editor_sidebar_line_items (declared in src/nimnui/platform/macos/platform.h), i.e. the sidebar's content model lives on the far side of the C boundary, where in Zed it is a gpui element list owned by the crate.
